Pulse beetle.damage: Larvae bore into pulses causing weight loss and quality reduction.
treatments: Sift infested grains and remove damaged ones.
Store at low humidity (<12%) and low temperature.
Use diatomaceous earth (food-grade) at recommended doses.
Consider neem-based botanical sprays for small-scale storage.
prevention: Use airtight containers or hermetic bags.

Rice weevil.damage: Creates bore holes and reduces grain weight; lays eggs inside grain.
treatments: Remove heavily infested lots; sun-dry the grains.
Apply diatomaceous earth or approved contact insecticide per label.
Store cereals in sealed containers and maintain low moisture.
prevention: Inspect new grain before mixing with old stock.

Storage pests in grains.damage: General contamination and damage by multiple species.
treatments: Remove visibly infested grains and sanitize storage.
Use cold storage (if feasible) for a few days to kill pests.
Consider professional fumigation for severe infestations.
prevention: Keep storage areas dry and clean.
Use mesh screens and sealed containers.

EGG.damage: Potential future infestation if eggs hatch.
treatments: Remove eggs manually if possible.
Sanitize and isolate affected grains.
Consider targeted low-toxicity treatment to prevent hatching.
prevention: Frequent monitoring; use sticky traps for adults.

LARVA.damage: High — larvae feed and make bore holes; can rapidly damage stock.
treatments: Isolate and destroy heavily infested samples.
Consider targeted biological control or approved insecticides.
Lower humidity and dry grains immediately.

Bore holes.damage: Indicator of activity inside grains; usually weevil or larval activity.
treatments: Inspect for live pests; discard heavily damaged grains.
Implement drying and sealing.
Consider professional fumigation for severe cases.

Grain - Rice weevil.damage: Visible external/embedded weevil damage on grains.
treatments: Remove damaged grains and sun-dry stock.
Use sealed, dry storage and monitor closely.
